newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Allied mulls options after rival merger.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Allied mulls options after rival merger.

text.p: Britain's ailing drinks to pub group Allied Domecq said on Tuesday it would appeal against the planned merger of rivals Grand Metropolitan Plc and Guinness if it was in shareholders' interests.
"If we think it's in shareholders interests to do so (we would appeal) but that is a function of what is going on in particular markets," Chairman Sir Christopher Hogg said in a conference call.
He declined to comment further on the question.

The deal, announced on Monday, creates the world's seventh largest branded food and drinks company called GMG Brands and the leading spirits and wine group with combined annual sales of more than 100 million cases.
Subject to European Union and United States regulatory approval, the merger also threatens to create a combined spirits division controlling half the Scotch Whisky business worldwide.

However, both joint chairmen of GMG Brands said on Monday they did not anticipate any problems from competition authorities, although Seagram the world's second largest spirits company branded the deal anti-competitive.
In the United States the joint spirits group is expected to sell three out of every four bottles of standard Scotch sold and one in every two bottles of premium gin.
But Hogg said it was "too early to comment in a nutshell" on the proposed 24 billion pound ($39 billion) merger.
"You will appreciate there is a need to analyse and think about many aspects of what is proposed."
However he said the merger may open up some opportunities for Allied.
"There will have to be rearrangements of distribution, sale of brands, management fall out. Not to mention the dislocation that occurs when two companies are put together."
The investment community believes the merger leaves Allied looking weak and in dire need of strategic partners if it is to stop its market share being eroded.

Earlier Allied announced first half results which showed a one percent fall in pretax profits at actual exchange rates to 317 million pounds, with profits from its spirits and wine division down two percent at 239 million pounds.

"We believe this weak result in spirits really brings Allied to the table," said SocGen analyst Nick Lyall. "The spirits business is struggling but you have to be aware of the takeover speculation now in play."

Allied shares were up 18p at 464p in early trade. The company said it expects its second half results to benefit from favourable spirits shipments to the United States and higher first half investment in its pub estate.

Sales of spirits in Europe were down three percent in the first half and in America one percent lower. In Europe volume increases in Spain and Germany were offset by declines in volume in Britain, Greece and Italy.

In Britain Teacher's whisky lost volume in the face of tougher pricing by competitors but sales of Courvoisier brandy improved. The company continued to concentrate its marketing effort on four core brands -- Ballantine's, Beefeater, Kahlua and Sauza.

Trading profit from the group's retailing division fell one percent to 105 million pounds with growth in its managed pubs like Big Steak Pubs and Firkin being offset by lower profits from off-licence chain Victoria Wine.
For the year as a whole the group estimates an adverse impact from currency translation of about 28 million pounds. ($ = 0.616 British Pounds)
